summary: Frontend-only verification of: (1) CRITICAL projectile/ground-illumination lighting regression fix, (2) weapon-dependent blood/gore color feature, (3) deep-space parallax enhancement, (4) quick regression on radial Skill Tree + Character panel. Ran ~7 fresh Playwright sessions through full char-creation -> tutorial-run gameplay -> firing -> kills, with screenshots at idle/firing/kill moments. RESULT: (1) lighting regression is GENUINELY FIXED — confirmed visually and via code review. (2) weapon-color gore feature is ONLY PARTIALLY implemented — a real bug found and root-caused (see below), blood visually still reads as mostly plain red. (3) parallax layers not visually confirmed reachable within normal play bounds (inconclusive, likely low-priority). (4) Skill Tree radial wheel + Character Attributes panel both open cleanly, zero console errors — regression PASS.

integration_issues.flow: Weapon-dependent blood/gore color (hydropistol #4dc4ff / runebolts #4dffd4 tutorial loadout)
integration_issues.issue: Feature only partially wired up — visually blood still reads as dominantly red/maroon during live gameplay (screenshots: kill_seq_0..5.png, hunt_scene.png, gameplay_after_move.png all show a large red/maroon particle cloud around hit/killed enemies despite both starting weapons being blue/teal). Root cause (engine.js): (a) dealDamage() line ~1541 `this.spawnBlood(e.x, e.y, e.t.color)` always uses the ENEMY's own color, not the weapon's bloodColor — this fires on every hit at 55% chance, independent of the new feature. (b) dealDamage() line ~1543 `this.spawnHitSparks(e.x, e.y, e.t.color, ...)` — same issue, always enemy color. (c) spawnBrutalKill()'s default 'gibs' death-blood-spray (line ~1676) only tints 1-in-5 particles with the weapon color (`i % 5 === 0 ? color : '#b51d28'`), the other 80% are hardcoded dark red `#b51d28` regardless of weapon — this is the dominant visual during a kill. (d) the 'bisect' fx path (line ~1658) has the identical 1-in-4 pattern. (e) `_curWeaponColor` is set inside `updateWeapons()`'s `for (const wid of owned)` loop every single frame — it gets overwritten by whichever weapon is iterated LAST in the owned-weapons array that frame, not tied to which weapon's projectile actually caused the hit being processed in dealDamage(). Since the tutorial loadout owns 2 weapons (hydropistol + runebolts) simultaneously, this is a real mis-attribution risk beyond just the red-tint issue.
affected_selectors: canvas (pixi renderer, no DOM selectors — gameplay canvas)

design_issues.screen: Deep-space parallax (mid nebula-cloud galaxies / far planet glow halo)
issues: Could not visually confirm the enhanced nebula-cloud/planet-glow layers within ~15s of continuous player movement in the tutorial run (only star field near-layer visible in all screenshots taken). This may simply be because the tutorial/wave arena is world-bounded and the camera never travels far enough in scaled parallax-space (mid layer uses factor 0.07, far layer 0.035) to trigger a visible cache rebuild within the arena's bounds. Code review of pixiRenderer.js confirms the enhancement code itself (layered soft nebula falloff circles + core star at lines ~582-597, atmospheric glow halo circle at line ~556) is present and looks correctly implemented on paper — this is a visibility/reachability observation, not a confirmed rendering bug. LOW priority, recommend a quick manual check in a longer/larger run if pixel-perfect confirmation is needed.

action_items: PRIORITY: Fix weapon-color gore — replace hardcoded '#b51d28' fallbacks in engine.js spawnBrutalKill() (both 'gibs' default path ~line 1676 and 'bisect' path ~line 1658) with the passed-in `color` param (100% of particles, not 1-in-4/1-in-5), OR at minimum increase weapon-color particle ratio so it's the dominant visual instead of the minority.

Fix dealDamage()'s spawnBlood(e.x, e.y, e.t.color) and spawnHitSparks(e.x, e.y, e.t.color, ...) calls (~lines 1541, 1543) to use the same `bloodColor` variable already computed on line 1516 instead of e.t.color, so per-hit blood/sparks (not just wound-threshold bursts) are also weapon-tinted.

Consider fixing _curWeaponColor attribution — currently set generically per-owned-weapon inside the updateWeapons() loop (overwritten each frame by loop order), not tied to which weapon's specific projectile caused the hit being processed. Recommend tagging projectiles with their own weapon color at spawn time (pr.color already exists per projectile per the ground-illum code) and reading pr.color directly in dealDamage() instead of relying on a single mutable _curWeaponColor.

Optional: verify deep-space nebula/planet parallax layers are actually reachable/visible within real (non-tutorial) run world bounds — could not visually confirm within this pass's exploration distance.
critical_code_review_comments: GOOD: The #1 priority lighting regression fix is correctly implemented exactly as described — _drawGroundIllum now uses this.lightTex (soft radial gradient) instead of this.litDiffuseTex (hard-edged), sized (pr.size||6)*3.4 with alpha 0.32, and the old always-on giant flashlight ground patch is gone. Verified visually: glow rings around hydropistol bolts are small (~15-30px), proportional to the player sprite, not a dominant blob. Zero console/WebGL/shader errors across all sessions including firing, moving, taking damage, and killing enemies.

BUG: Weapon-dependent gore color is inconsistently applied across ~5 different particle-spawning call sites in engine.js (spawnBlood, spawnHitSparks, spawnBrutalKill's two fx branches) — only spawnWoundBurst (10%-HP-threshold bursts) and the final pushBloodDecal/killEnemy path reliably use the weapon color; the higher-frequency/higher-volume calls (every-hit blood splatter, death blood spray) mostly default to a hardcoded red, which is why the net visual impression during actual play is still 'plain red blood' — this directly contradicts the explicit user ask ('instead of always plain red').

DESIGN SMELL: _curWeaponColor as a single engine-wide mutable field set inside a per-frame loop over ALL owned weapons is fragile — will misattribute color whenever a player owns 2+ weapons (which is the normal end-game/mid-game state, and even true in the tutorial loadout tested here). A per-projectile color lookup (pr.color, which already exists) is the more correct approach and is already used correctly in _drawGroundIllum.

success_rate.frontend: ~75% — critical #1 lighting-size regression confirmed FIXED (highest priority item, PASS); Skill Tree + Character panel regression PASS; weapon-color gore feature FAILS visual verification (real bug, root-caused); deep-space parallax enhancement not visually confirmed (inconclusive, likely non-blocking)

test_credentials: Not needed — localStorage-only guest flow (key 'wds.save.v1'), no login required.
seed_data_creation: Seeded via localStorage in several sessions per instructions: sp:80, profile.level:6, introSeen:true, tutorialDone:true (the latter two flags are required to reach Camp instead of replaying the AIDA intro dialogue on reload, per prior iteration_19 finding).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro steps for the gore-color bug: create a character, click ENTER THE LAKE, click through the ~4-step AIDA intro dialogue (tap anywhere ~10-12 times), then hold left-click while aiming at any green 'slime' enemy cluster and move with WASD to approach them. Within a few seconds you'll get a CRIT hit and/or a kill — take a screenshot immediately; the blood/wound particle burst will visually read as predominantly reddish/maroon (#b51d28) even though the tutorial loadout is hydropistol (#4dc4ff, pale blue) + runebolts (#4dffd4, teal), neither of which is red. Confirmed via code review (not just visual impression) that ~80% of the main death-blood-spray particles and 100% of the every-hit spawnBlood/spawnHitSparks calls use hardcoded/enemy colors instead of the weapon color, per action_items above. The #1 priority lighting-size regression, however, IS genuinely fixed — small proportional glow rings confirmed via screenshots (see gameplay_firing_1.png, kill_seq_*.png in .screenshots dir), zero console/WebGL errors across every session.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of gore-color bug: the weapon-color threading was only added to a subset of the ~5 particle-emission call sites involved in a single hit/kill (spawnWoundBurst + killEnemy's final decal), while the higher-frequency/higher-volume call sites (dealDamage's direct spawnBlood/spawnHitSparks calls, and spawnBrutalKill's default 'gibs'/'bisect' death-spray branches) were left referencing the pre-existing hardcoded '#b51d28' / e.t.color values from before this feature was added. Net visual effect: the weapon-tinted particles are present but are a small minority mixed into a majority of red/enemy-colored particles, so the human eye reads the overall gore as still 'basically red'. Mitigation: thread the already-computed `bloodColor`/`color` param through the remaining 3-4 call sites listed in action_items.
